extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians (readers of Mochizuki/IUT) interested in the logical structure of inter-universal Teichmüller theory and related gluing constructions
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of the logical/structural requirements and pitfalls that arise in gluing constructions and in the interpretation of logical relators (AND/OR/XOR) in inter-universal Teichmüller theory. Covers examples, analogies (line segments, group indices, carry operations), and consequences of identifying 'redundant copies'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish logical AND “∧” vs. logical OR “∨”
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential mathematical content of examples may be reformulated in terms of AND “∧” and OR “∨”; identifying whether a relation is an AND or an OR is central to correct interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (AOL1)–(AOL4) illustrate situations where ∧ holds for one configuration but, after identifying certain copies, only ∨ holds and ∧ fails. The choice affects whether constructions (e.g., Θ-link, multiradial representation) are meaningful/nontrivial. Keep track of whether statements assert simultaneous validity (∧) or alternative possibilities (∨).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not confuse narrative ∧/∨ with logical ∧/∨
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of narratively considering multiple cases in exposition (a 'narrative AND' or 'narrative OR') is not the same as asserting a logical conjunction or disjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.4 (Nar1, Nar2) gives a fallacious argument resulting from treating the narrative act of considering both cases x=3 and x=1 as if x both equals 3 and equals 1. Ensure that case-splitting in exposition is not mistaken for simultaneous truth of cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying 'redundant copies' can transform ∧-relations into ∨-relations
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of identifying distinct labeled copies (e.g., †I and ‡I) can change a situation where an AND relation holds into one where only an OR relation holds, and the original AND fails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.1 and discussion: identifying labels (motivated by perceived redundancy) may force passage from an AND-world to an OR-world (and introduce indeterminacy). When considering identifications, check whether this invalidates simultaneous conditions that previously held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions may fail to glue across identified components unless values are unambiguous
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate functions on distinct copies need not glue to a well-defined single-valued function on the glued object if their values disagree on the overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AOD1/AOD2: coordinate 'x' on two copies †I, ‡I might not glue to an R-valued function on J because the value on the overlap γJ may be ambiguous (0 or 1). One may instead need to view values in a glued target like †,‡R. Check pointwise compatibility of values on overlaps before asserting existence of a global function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentials (or other sheaf-theoretic objects) can glue where functions cannot
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when functions fail to glue, associated differentials (e.g., 'dx') on the components may glue to a single well-defined differential on the glued object and be compatible with quotient maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AOD3: the differentials 'dx' on the two copies glue to a single differential on J and arise as the pullback from the quotient J → M. Use sheaf/compatibility checks: differentials, cohomological objects, or pullbacks may be better behaved under gluing than naive functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indices of subgroups become indeterminate up to powers when labels are collapsed
rubrics_metrics.description: After identifying labeled copies in diagrams of groups, subgroup indices [Gi : Gj] may only be well-defined up to multiplication by integral powers of n (i.e., become indeterminate elements of the multiplicative subgroup generated by n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.3 (iv): collapsing labels yields each index only defined up to n^m ambiguity. When computing indices after identifications, record possible multiplicative indeterminacies rather than asserting strict equalities that held before identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain distinct labels for distinct objects when they play structurally different roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Using distinct labels (e.g., G1, G2, G3 or digits D1, D2, D3) is essential to correctly represent carry operations, indices, and other structural distinctions; deleting labels can invalidate strict computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.6: distinct digit labels are fundamental to base-n arithmetic carry computations; deleting labels can lead to contradictions unless one introduces quotients/indeterminacy. However, for some specific algorithms one may get results matching up to bounded discrepancy (e.g., modulo n−1). Explicitly track labels when they encode structural data.

rubrics_metrics.name: The AND-property of the Θ-link is central for meaningful multiradial constructions (AND-IUT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter-universal Teichmüller constructions (Θ-link, multiradial representation, final numerical estimate) are meaningful/nontrivial precisely because the Θ-link is interpreted as a logical AND relation (distinct parameters are allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.5 (ii): the multiradial representation and the derivation of numerical estimates rely on treating the defining data as simultaneously valid (∧). Misinterpreting the Θ-link as ∨ (OR-IUT) or collapsing distinct parameters can render the constructions vacuous or force indeterminacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid arbitrary shifts from ∧ to ∨ in different stages of an argument (EssOR-IUT pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting an AND-interpretation at the definitional level but switching to an OR-interpretation later (or vice versa) without justification leads to abrupt/mysterious/unjustified transitions in conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.5 (iii),(vi): EssOR-IUT is described as accepting ∧ formally but shifting to ∨ in the multiradial stage; such an arbitrary shift makes the logical structure vacuous or unjustified. Maintain consistent logical interpretation across stages unless a rigorous reason for change is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical implication direction matters: ∧ ⇒ ∨ but ∨ (generally) not ⇒ ∧
rubrics_metrics.description: Formally, conjunction implies disjunction, but the converse is not valid; in the context of passing from ∨-versions to ∧-versions of constructions, such a transition is generally impossible or unjustified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.5 (vii): one cannot in general pass from a ∨-version of the multiradial representation to an ∧-version; any such purported passage must be checked for hidden assumptions. Treat attempts to infer simultaneous truths from disjunctive data with skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing along multiplicative group schemes may not preserve ring-scheme structures; regular vs rational functions differ across the gluing
rubrics_metrics.description: A gluing of ring schemes along group-scheme isomorphisms can produce compatibility for multiplicative structures without compatibility for additive/ring structures; regular functions need not match but rational functions may.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.7 (ii–iii): in the standard projective line gluing, there is an isomorphism of multiplicative group schemes that does not extend to ring-scheme isomorphisms; regular functions on one side do not directly translate to regular functions on the other, whereas rational functions do. When gluing, check which structural sheaves and operations are preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting labels in a gluing forces introduction of quotients/indeterminacy (∨) to avoid contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: If one removes distinguishing labels from components in a gluing that relied on labels, the result typically contradicts strict equalities (e.g., T ≠ T^{−1}) unless one moves to a quotient/collection of possibilities — i.e., an OR/indeterminacy interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.7 (ii-h) and related discussions: the 'gluing without labels' leads to contradiction unless one accepts an indeterminacy/quotient. When simplifying by erasing labels, make explicit the resulting loss of information and the kind of indeterminacy introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use carry-OR (¨∨) as an analytic analogy for mixed-characteristic 'stacked' operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventional mixed-characteristic/carry addition (mod 4) can be described as a 'carry-OR' operator ¨∨ which stacks multiplication (∧) on top of addition (XOR) in F2: ¨∨ = (∧, ˙∨).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 2.4.6 (iii): view some mixed-characteristic phenomena as 'stacked' Boolean operations. This analogy can clarify how multiplicative and additive structures interact under lifts (Teichmüller representatives) and why multiplicative compatibility may hold while additive compatibility fails. Use it to reason about behavior of operations under gluing and reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer structural/sheaf-theoretic checks (pullbacks, compatibility with quotient maps) over naive componentwise identifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether objects glue or are compatible under identifications is often decided by sheaf-theoretic/pullback compatibility (e.g., differentials arise as pullbacks), not by naive label identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout Examples AOD3, projective-line discussion, and Θ-link analogies: verify compatibility via pullback/pushforward, sheaf/gluing data, and poly-isomorphism conditions rather than by simply identifying labelled copies. This avoids hidden indeterminacies and unjustified equivalences.
